articles.title: Oak Ridge Boys’ Richard Sterban, Whose Distinctive Bass Voice Powered ‘Elvira’ and Other Country Smashes, Dies at 83
articles.summary: Richard Sterban, the bass vocalist of the Oak Ridge Boys, died Saturday in Hendersonville, Tenn., following complications from bronchitis and pneumonia after a battle with cancer. He was 83. Both his family and the band announced his death. “We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers.
body: Sterban joined the Oak Ridge Boys as the group’s bass singer in 1972 after previous member Noel Fox left the band. Alongside lead singer Duane Allen, baritone William Lee Golden and tenor Joe Bonsall, Sterban helped complete the gospel quartet. The group placed 34 singles in the country Top 10, 17 of them at No. 1, earned Grammy, Country Music Association and Academy of Country Music awards, and became members of the Grand Ole Opry, the Gospel Music Hall of Fame and the Country Music Hall of Fame. Sterban’s voice was the foundation of the group’s four-part harmonies, particularly apparent on the famous song “Elvira,” among others.

Before he joined the Oak Ridge Boys, he helped found the Keystones, a gospel quartet, before joining J.D. Sumner and the Stamps Quartet, which Elvis Presley hired to sing behind him for about a year and a half.

Sterban was born April 24, 1943, in Camden, New Jersey. He began singing at age six in Sunday school and sang tenor in his seventh-grade glee club. After graduating from Collingswood High School, he studied music at Trenton State College.

Both his family and the band announced his death.

articles.title: Inside the First AI Music Awards, a Chaotic Evening Attempting to Normalize Tech-Assisted Tunes
articles.summary: I knew things were a little off when the first thing I heard on my walk to the AI Music Awards was “the winner…” followed by the sweet voice of Kelly Clarkson. No, Miss American Idol did not abandon her feud with the Brooklyn bird to capitalize on her newfound appreciation for AI. But as
body: To qualify for the awards, artists needed to register their tracks to SIQA’s “Verified Registry,” which denotes whether the song was fully AI-generated, made with the assistance of AI or featured a cloned human voice to lead the tune (what the group calls a “human + AI hybrid”).

The Sonic Intelligence Academy is the brainchild of software engineer Timirah “TJ” James and her sister Mia James. Since its January launch, it has worked to establish an awards program to counter the mainstream music industry’s aversion to AI. The group believes there needs to be infrastructure that supports those using AI to create music, rather than dismissing its existence, and it hopes to be an AI counterpart to the longstanding Recording Academy that governs the Grammy Awards. It advocates for artists to publicly associate themselves with their AI-powered work, eager to highlight the humans who helped create the product.

articles.title: Chris Pratt Says He ‘Would Love’ James Gunn to Direct a Fourth ‘Guardians of the Galaxy’ Film After DC Exit
articles.summary: Chris Pratt thinks it would be “awesome” to reunite with James Gunn for a fourth “Guardians of the Galaxy” film after the director announced his departure from DC Studios this week. Gunn and his co-chief, Peter Safran, were ousted from their positions on Nov.
body: The executive shuffle marks another setback for DC Studios, which has struggled to compete with the powerhouse that is Disney’s Marvel Cinematic Universe of late. But it opens a route for Gunn to return to the MCU, where he directed three “Guardians of the Galaxy” movies.

Pratt recently told Moviezine that he would love to reunite with Gunn for a fourth film in the franchise. “That would be awesome. I love working with James. He’s the man,” Pratt said when asked about the possibility of making the film. “I haven’t had a chance to speak with him since that news came out yesterday…. It’s always tough because anytime something like this comes up, it could always become a headline.”
He continued: “All I’ll say is I love James. He directed all three movies, and that’s pretty rare… so if he wanted to come back and bring it back, I would love that.”

Pratt has starred as Star-Lord in the franchise across six films, with 2014’s “Guardians of the Galaxy,” “Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2,” “Avengers: Infinity War,” “Avengers: Endgame,” “Thor: Love and Thunder” and most recently in “Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3.”

articles.title: Hannah Fry feels 'unbelievably lucky' after cervical cancer treatment
articles.summary: The presenter says she has received a 'five-year clear' after having a hysterectomy in her thirties.
body: Prof Hannah Fry has described feeling "unbelievably lucky" after being treated for cervical cancer.
The mathematician and BBC presenter, who recently took part in the second season of the Celebrity Traitors, said cancerous cells were discovered after she attended a cervical screening in 2020.
She underwent a hysterectomy, describing the experience to BBC Radio 4's Desert Island Discs as "horrific".
"As awful as that was, it had a full stop at the end of the sentence," the 42-year-old added. "I had my five-year clear the other day. I feel so unbelievably lucky."

articles.title: Philippines Wins Inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Thailand
articles.summary: The Philippines has won the first ever Eurovision Song Contest Asia. Carmelle, representing the Phillippines, scooped first place with the track “Sobra-Sobra,” earning 211 points.
body: The first ever Asian edition of the contest was held Saturday in the Thai capital of Bangkok. Eleven countries took part, including Cambodia, Mongolia and Korea. Like the European edition, which recently celebrated 70 years, points were awarded via a combination of national juries and public vote.
A “rest of the world” vote also awarded a set of points equivalent to that of one participating country, with audiences from 183 countries and territories worldwide having their say.

The contest was aired in the participating countries as well as on Eurovision’s official YouTube channel. EBU members TVP (Poland), Sveriges Radio (Sweden), Kan (Israel) and SBS (Australia) also broadcast the contest, which was hosted by Thai TV stars Woody Milintachinda and Cindy Bishop.

As well as the competing countries, Thai superstar Jeff Satur performed alongside this year’s Eurovision winner Dara, who took first place for Bulgaria in the May contest with her track “Bangaranga.” The show, which also included a special opening performance celebrating the host city, was produced by Voxovation and Bangkok-based S20 Productions. It was sponsored by Zoop.

articles.title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'
articles.summary: The singer felt forced to compete with her female peers, until she realised the power of longevity.
body: You might know her as a pop star, endorsed by everyone from Taylor Swift to Sam Fender, but Holly Humberstone has a secret double life.
"We've stolen one of our neighbours' cats by accident," she laughs, in a Zoom call from her fixer-upper in New Cross, south-east London.
"He's a tiny little black cat who's come into our garden and simply chosen us."
Under the slightest scrutiny, however, her story crumbles like a biscuit in a hot cup of tea.

articles.title: ‘I relive that mission every single day of my life’: how Black soldiers handled the Vietnam war
articles.summary: In ambitious documentary Soul Patrol, the complicated experiences of the Vietnam war’s first Black special ops team are explored both on and off the battleground. Ask the average American to name an elite US fighting force, and they might kick off with the Rangers or the Seals.
body: Known as long-range reconnaissance patrols, or LRRPs, these small teams of six to eight soldiers were dropped behind enemy lines to track supply routes and hostile positions, sometimes for days at a time. Stealth was essential. Their job was to identify targets and call in the cavalry, usually in the form of airstrikes, while avoiding direct engagement with enemy forces to preserve their cover.

A melancholy new documentary reckons with the weight of it all. Directed by Harper, Soul Patrol uncovers this hidden chapter of US military history: the story of army team 2/6 of company F, 51st infantry, the Vietnam war’s first Black special operations team – a ragtag bunch of daredevils and dreamers who snuck into the jungle, stared down death and lived to tell a tale that has taken half a century to share in living color. Based on a 2003 war memoir of the same name, the film follows author Ed Emanuel as he assembles the team for a gathering that edges from high school reunion to PTSD group therapy session.
The survivor’s guilt has haunted the team ever since. “I relive that mission every single day of my life,” Emanuel says. “We survived the war, but there was no peace.”

articles.title: Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys’ Bass Singer, Dies at 83
articles.summary: Sterban died in Hendersonville, Tennessee, to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia after fighting a battle with cancer, his family and the music group announced.
body: Richard Sterban, the Oak Ridge Boys’ bass singer who memorably lent his vocals to their beloved “Elvira” cover, died Saturday. He was 83.
Sterban died in Hendersonville, Tennessee, due to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia after fighting a battle with cancer, his family and the Oak Ridge Boys announced.

Born on April 24, 1943, in Camden, New Jersey, Sterban began singing at 6 in Sunday school as a soprano. He sang tenor in his seventh-grade glee club, and upon his eighth grade, his voice dropped to bass.
He studied music at Trenton State College (modernly known as the College of New Jersey), and began singing in a gospel quartet where he met Joe Bonsall, his future Oak Ridge Boys bandmate.

articles.title: Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
articles.summary: Front-runner Carmelle emerges victorious with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra.
body: The Philippines have won the very first Eurovision Song Contest Asia, hosted in Bangkok and with 11 countries vying for the title.
She earned 211 points in total - 93 from the jury and 118 from the public vote - ahead of Thailand's MANG x DAOU in second place with 170 points.
There was a joyous atmosphere at the One Bangkok Arena as the crowd cheered the contestants and celebrated the popular winner.
Carmelle, the youngest contestant in the competition, was an obvious favourite with the juries and the public despite strong showings from several nations.

articles.title: Chris Pratt “Would Love” to Make a Fourth ‘Guardians of the Galaxy’ Film With James Gunn “If He Wanted to” Amid DC Exit
articles.summary: "I love working with James [Gunn]. He’s the man. I haven’t had a chance to speak with him since that news came out," the actor said of Gunn's exit from DC Studios.
body: Chris Pratt “would love” to make a fourth Guardians of the Galaxy movie if James Gunn wanted to revisit the Marvel film franchise after his exit from DC Studios.

Pratt starred as Star-Lord/Peter Quill in all three Guardians of the Galaxy films for Marvel alongside Zoe Saldaña, Karen Gillan, Dave Bautista, Vin Diesel and Bradley Cooper. Pom Klementieff joined the cast in its second installment.

Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 released in 2023, and was meant to be the final film in the Guardians franchise. Before the movie came out, it was revealed that Gunn and Peter Safran were set to become co-chairs and co-CEOs of DC Studios. It was announced last Monday that the duo will be replaced by Marvel alum Jeremy Latcham, who will now serve as president and chief creative officer of DC Studios.

Gunn and Safran were presumed safe from being removed from their posts at DC Studios amid the merge of Paramount and Warner Bros., though Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz opted to bring Latcham in.
